body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_{jh}(w)=Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{j,T_j+h}-\sum_{i\in D_{jh}}w_{jh,i}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,T_j+h}\), with honest-width frontier \(W_s\) and fixed-Bonferroni SOCP value \(\Gamma_s\) for \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\)

sampling_model.design: Condition on fixed integer dimensions, deterministic adoption dates with \(\mathcal J\ne\varnothing\), rational predictors and class radii, a known rational covariance factor, and a certified rational Bonferroni multiplier.
sampling_model.units: The finite set \(\mathcal I\) contains treated, not-yet-treated, and never-treated units; repeated unit--calendar-time cells are deduplicated in \(Q\).
sampling_model.treatment: Adoption is absorbing and deterministic; \(D_{jh}=\{i:T_i>T_j+h\}\) identifies untreated donor outcomes at the relevant calendar time.
sampling_model.overlap: The treated set is nonempty, and every deepest donor pool \(D_{jK}\) is nonempty; nesting then makes every horizon-specific donor simplex feasible and gives \(M\geq1\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no random nuisance estimation: weights and half-widths depend only on fixed design and model inputs. On the zero-bias class, the general correlated exact frontier is characterized through the known-covariance Gaussian-cube quantile; numerical correlated Gaussian-max calibration remains a post-solve refinement. The diagonal row-disjoint specialization reduces calibration to one explicit product equation.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper defines shrinking not-yet-treated donor sets and focuses its exposition and application on the common deepest-horizon pool, while explicitly noting that its estimator may instead use horizon-varying donor sets; it does not supply this note's bounded-mean known-covariance class or evaluate the width programs here.
The paper offers non-asymptotic staggered synthetic-control prediction intervals, conic implementations, and uniform inference across post-treatment periods.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals for scalar linear functionals over convex regression classes under known-variance Gaussian errors.
The paper trades worst-case conditional imbalance against variance when constructing generalized optimal matching weights.
The paper constructs facial-reduced extended duals with strong duality when ordinary conic constraint qualifications fail.
The paper gives necessary and sufficient closed-cone conditions for Farkas lemmas and strong duality in second-order-cone programming.

body.tldr: Staggered adoption creates shrinking sets of not-yet-treated donors. Conditional on a nonempty rationally encoded fixed design, this note turns all treated-unit--horizon errors into one deduplicated Gaussian contrast vector, derives the exact worst-case bias radius, and chooses horizon-specific simplex weights with a fixed-Bonferroni SOCP. The resulting band is finite-sample honest and lies within a dimension-uniform factor of the best deterministic linear synthetic-control rectangle. On the zero-bias class, the exact correlated-Gaussian frontier is the minimum over feasible weights of the centered Gaussian-cube quantile, and a nonzero Loewner covariance reduction at a deep optimizer gives a strict nested-width gain. Diagonal covariance with disjoint eligible row cells yields the explicit Gaussian-product root, and the two-horizon witness has a proved strict exact-width gap as well as a strict \(\Gamma\) gap. The facial-reduction theorem separately gives a complete degeneracy-safe if-and-only-if certificate for strict \(\Gamma\) improvement. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein supply donor geometry only, not this statistical class or an evaluated estimator.

project_justification.gap: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein define the shrinking donor sets and focus their exposition and application on \(D_{jK}\), while explicitly noting that their estimator may use horizon-varying donors. This note uses that geometry but neither attributes its bounded-mean Gaussian class to them nor claims that either width program evaluates their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik supply non-asymptotic simultaneous prediction and conic architecture but do not optimize the exact honest joint width over the two nested products of donor simplexes. Scalar convex-class interval theory does not give the correlated Gaussian-cube variational frontier, its strict Loewner criterion, the independent-coordinate product root, or the degeneracy-safe comparison of the two SOCPs.
project_justification.niche: Known covariance with a prespecified spectral band, rational fixed inputs, a nonempty treated set, and this note's bounded linear conditional-mean class isolate a finite-sample panel decision problem in which donor availability, worst-case bias, shared-cell covariance, multiplicity, and exact comparison are explicit. The targets are the attainable honest-width frontier \(W_s\), its implementable fixed-Bonferroni surrogate \(\Gamma_s\), and auditable strict-improvement tests for each object on its proved domain.
project_justification.fill: The note derives a deduplicated contrast representation, an exact support-function bias radius, finite-sample honest SOCP bands, and a dimension-uniform comparison with the exact robust frontier. It characterizes \(W_s\) on the zero-bias correlated-Gaussian class as an attained covariance-quantile optimization, proves a strict Loewner covariance criterion, specializes it to an explicit independent-coordinate product root, proves a strict exact-width gain in the rational staggered witness, and proves a separate finite if-and-only-if facial-reduction certificate for strict \(\Gamma\) improvement on degenerate active faces.

body.related_work: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, Section 2, paragraphs defining \(\mathcal D_{jk}\)) provide the shrinking-donor-set geometry and focus their exposition and application on the deepest pool \(D_{jK}\), while explicitly noting that their estimator may instead use horizon-varying donor sets. They do not supply this note's bounded-mean known-covariance class, and no theorem here evaluates or dominates their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025, Sections 4.4 and 6 and Supplemental Appendix S.6) provide prediction-error, simultaneous-coverage, and conic-programming architecture; the present frontier changes the decision variable and loss. Armstrong and Koles\'ar (2018, equation (13) and Sections 3.2--3.4) provide scalar worst-case-bias plus standard-error logic over a convex Gaussian regression class. Anderson (1955, Theorem 1) supplies the weak ray-monotonic moving-set inequality; this note derives the strict bounded-cube consequence for a nonzero, possibly singular covariance increment and applies it to the optimized staggered-donor frontier. Kallus (2020) motivates the dual-norm bias--variance optimization analogy. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015, Theorems 2 and 3) supply Gaussian comparison tools for the general constant-factor result, while the global spectral covariance band is this note's explicit finite-experiment restriction. Pataki (2013, Sections 3--4), Jeyakumar, Kum, and Lee (2008, Theorems 3.1 and 4.1), and exact real-algebraic elimination support the proved degeneracy-safe certificate theorem \(\texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate}\). Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021), Cao, Lu, and Wu (2026), Cerulli (2024), and Wei, Park, Kalangi, and Huang (2026) address different prediction, long-panel, donor-selection, or calibration regimes.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact robust frontier \(W_s\) and the implementable SOCP value \(\Gamma_s\) remain distinct. On the zero-bias class, the correlated frontier now has an attained Gaussian-cube quantile characterization and a strict Loewner-order criterion; computing general correlated Gaussian-max quantiles remains a post-solve refinement. The rational witness proves strict improvement for both objects through the diagonal row-disjoint specialization. Outside covariance comparability at a deep optimizer, the paper proves weak support dominance and the dimension-uniform comparison, not that every strict \(\Gamma\) gap is a strict \(W\) gap. The facial-reduction equivalence \(\texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate}\) concerns strict \(\Gamma\) improvement on arbitrary degenerate active faces.
body.honest_scope: Finite-sample coverage, the covariance-domination sandwich, the constant-factor frontier, weak nested-support dominance, and the two-horizon strict witness are theorem-level results. On the zero-bias class, \(\texttt{thm:correlated-gaussian-exact-frontier}\) gives an attained exact-width variational formula and a strict Loewner covariance criterion. On its diagonal row-disjoint specialization, \(\texttt{thm:disjoint-diagonal-exact-frontier}\) gives the explicit product root, and \(\texttt{prop:strict-witness-exact-frontier-gap}\) gives a proved positive exact-width gap. The complete finite certificate on degenerate SOCP faces is proved by \(\texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate}\); it is not an open OEQ and is not a substitute for exact-\(W\) strictness. The covariance band is a prespecified restriction for the known-covariance finite experiment. Unknown covariance, random donor selection, outcome-dependent weights, numerical general correlated Gaussian-max calibration, and a direct comparison with the Ben-Michael--Feller--Rothstein partially pooled estimator are outside this version. When donor sets coincide, the two support rules reduce to the same problem; with one unbiased contrast, the SOCP reduces to a rationally certified classical known-covariance Gaussian interval.
body.interpretation: The strict witness isolates the value of an early donor that is untreated when the early effect is measured but adopts by the final horizon. Allowing that donor only where valid lowers the early minimum variance from \(3/2\) to \(4/3\) without changing the late variance \(3/200\). The exact Gaussian-product characterization converts that local variance reduction into a proved strict simultaneous-width reduction, without relying on a numerical interval certificate. More generally, a nested feasible covariance that is strictly smaller in Loewner order than the deep optimum yields a strict exact-width gain even with correlated contrasts and a singular covariance difference. These are statements about deterministic linear bands in the declared experiment, not about the numerical output or statistical class of an existing partially pooled synthetic-control estimator.
